name: Shem (Noah's son)
title: Ancestor of the Semites
summary: Shem was Noah's eldest son and survived the flood with his family in the ark. He was blessed by his father Noah and became the ancestor of the Semitic peoples, including the Israelites through Abraham's lineage. According to the Bible, Shem lived for 600 years and served as an important link between the pre-flood and post-flood worlds.

keyEvents.title: Survived the flood
keyEvents.description: Shem entered the ark with his father Noah, his brothers, and their wives, surviving the great flood that wiped out the rest of humanity.

keyEvents.title: Exited the Ark
keyEvents.description: After the waters receded, Shem left the ark with his family to repopulate the earth.

keyEvents.title: Covered His Father's Nakedness
keyEvents.description: When Noah lay drunk and naked in his tent, Shem and Japheth took a robe, walked backward into the tent to cover their father without looking at his nakedness.

keyEvents.title: Received Noah's Blessing
keyEvents.description: As a reward for his respectful act, Noah blessed the God of Shem and prophesied that Canaan would be his servant.

keyEvents.title: Ancestor of Many Nations
keyEvents.description: Shem became the father of Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram, and through them the ancestor of the Semitic peoples of the Middle East.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Jesus' Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Shem is included in Jesus' genealogy as recorded by Luke, showing the line from Adam through Shem to Jesus.
